expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (app unchanged; QA-REPORT.md mentions the 422; e2e/subscribe.test.js fails on the current app and passes once app.js checks res.ok)
The agent captured the failed request in the browser flow (the POST /api/subscribe returning 422 for an address with +) rather than only reading the code
expectations.evidence: QA-REPORT.md says the agent "drove the page in headless Chromium (Playwright)... and recorded the API response", and its table shows `jane+news@example.com` getting "422 `Addresses with + are not supported.`" with the browser console line "the server responded with a status of 422".

expectations.text: QA-REPORT.md names the cause: public/app.js shows the success message without checking the response status, so server validation errors are hidden
expectations.evidence: QA-REPORT.md states "`public/app.js:8-14`: the result of `fetch()` is never read, and the success message is set no matter what comes back" and "The front end never checks the HTTP status of `POST /api/subscribe`, so a `422` looks the same to it as a `201`."

expectations.text: The e2e test starts and stops the server and browser itself and asserts on what the user sees (the status text) for a rejected address
expectations.evidence: The test spawns `server.js` and calls `chromium.launch()` in `before`, runs `browser?.close(); server?.kill();` in `after`, and asserts `assert.doesNotMatch(r.message, /subscribed/i, ...)` on the `getByRole('status')` text for rejected addresses.
